hints.alg.inequality-graphs.graph: Dot at the number: closed (filled) for ≤ or ≥, open for < or >. Shade toward the numbers that make it true: right for greater, left for less. If the number comes first (3 < x), read it from x's side (x > 3).
hints.alg.inequality-graphs.read: Open dot: < or >. Closed dot: ≤ or ≥. Shaded right: x is greater; shaded left: x is less.
hints.alg.inequality-graphs.compound: "And" (or a chain like −2 < x ≤ 4): shade between the dots. "Or": shade outward from each dot. Closed dots for ≤ and ≥.
hints.alg.inequality-graphs: Closed dot for ≤ or ≥, open for < or >. Shade toward the numbers that work; between for and, outward for or.

misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-graph-dot: Check the dots: closed (filled) means the number is included (≤ or ≥); open means it isn't (< or >).
misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-graph-direction: Check the shading: greater than goes right (bigger numbers); less than goes left.
misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-graph-reversed: The number comes first here. 3 < x means x > 3: read it from x's side, then shade.
misconceptionMessages.alg.compound-and-or: "And" means both are true at once: between the dots. "Or" means either one: outward from both dots.

sections.title: Graph an inequality
sections.objective: Graph x > 3 or −2 ≥ x on a number line.
explain: An inequality has many answers: every number on one side of a boundary. The graph shows them all.
Tap the line to put a dot, tap the dot again to make it open, then choose the shading.

examples.why: Open dot: 3 itself isn't more than 3. Shade right: 4, 5, 3.5 … all work.
Closed dot: −2 is included (or equal to). Shade left, toward smaller numbers.
The number comes first: read it from x's side. x is bigger than 1, so shade right.

sections.key: Dot at the number: closed for ≤ or ≥ (included), open for < or > (not included). Shade toward the numbers that work: right for greater, left for less.

sections.title: Read a graph
sections.objective: Write the inequality a graph shows.
explain: Work backwards: the dot gives the number, open or closed gives < or ≤, and the shading gives the direction.
sections.key: Open dot: < or >. Closed dot: ≤ or ≥. Shaded right: x is greater. Shaded left: x is less.

sections.title: Compound inequalities
sections.objective: Graph −2 < x ≤ 4 and x < −1 or x ≥ 3, solving first when needed.
explain: A compound inequality joins two: "and" means both must be true (between), "or" means either one (outward).
To solve −3 ≤ 2x + 1 < 7, do the same to all three parts.

examples.why: Both at once: x is between −2 and 4. Open at −2, closed at 4.
Either one: everything left of −1 and everything from 3 up. The middle doesn't work.
Subtract 1 from all three parts, then divide all three by 2.

sections.key: "And" (or a chain like −2 < x ≤ 4): shade between the dots. "Or": shade outward from both. Closed dots for ≤ and ≥, open for < and >.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Graphing, reading and compound inequalities, mixed.
sections.key: Closed dot for ≤ or ≥, open for < or >. Shade toward the numbers that work: between for and, outward for or.
